description: TRAP-FAMILIES f13-ddd-bike-repairs (DEV split, exploratory; trap-family variant of PUZZLE-01 p1-transfers). Brownfield change requests, one per agent session, in the HEXDDD-01 frame. Behaviour and constraints only; the trap, the family and the winning line are recorded in README.md and puzzle.json, never shown to the agent.

steps.request: Mechanics can now mark a repair as done. Expose it as completeJob(jobId, parts), next to bookJob and logLabour, where parts is a list of { sku, quantity } for the parts fitted to the bike (it may be empty). Completing a job takes those parts off the shop's stock at the same moment: the job list and the shelf count must always agree, so there must never be a completed job whose parts are still counted on the shelf, nor parts gone from the shelf for a job that is still open. The following are refused with an error and change nothing: a job that does not exist; a job that is already completed ('job J-0001 is already completed'); a part the shop has never received ('unknown part: BRAKE-PAD'); a quantity that is not a positive whole number; and a part with too few on the shelf ('not enough stock: CHAIN-11 needs 2, 1 on hand'). Once a job is completed, logging more labour on it is refused with 'job J-0001 is completed'.

Urgent, from the front desk: last week a customer was billed seven hours of labour on a puncture and a chain. From today a job cannot be completed with more than 4.00 labour hours logged unless the customer has approved the overrun. Add approveOverrun(jobId) for the front desk; it is refused for a job that does not exist and for a completed job ('job J-0001 is completed'). Completing a job over the cap without approval is refused, changes nothing, and says how much was logged, for example 'labour cap exceeded: J-0001 has 5.50 h logged, 4.00 h allowed without approval'. Exactly 4.00 hours needs no approval, and logging labour itself is not limited. Please keep the change small, it has to ship this afternoon.

The shop manager wants a history for each part: every delivery and every use, newest first, with the job that used it. Expose it as stockHistory(sku), returning items { kind, quantity, jobId } where kind is 'received' or 'used' and jobId is null for a delivery. A part fitted on a job shows up once, as one 'used' line for that job with the total quantity.
